Strong track record of organizational leadership, including coaching leaders, driving change, and building high-performing teams. Position Summary: The Strategic Finance Analytics Manager is a newly created role that builds and leads the financial modelling and analytics capability at the core of PointClickCare’s strategic finance function. The role delivers the models, tools, and decision support that enable leadership to drive profitability, optimize commercial strategy, and allocate resources with precision — with work that is highly visible to executive leadership, the Board, and investors. Build and maintain in-house financial and profitability models that evaluate the revenue and margin implications of strategic decisions, beginning with pricing and commercial strategy and expanding to other strategic finance domains. Run scenario and sensitivity analyses on packaging, pricing changes, GTM strategies, and investment trade-offs, measured against NRR, ARR, and contribution margin. AI-Led Modernization of the Analytics Toolkit. Apply AI/ML tools, including LLMs and predictive modelling, to accelerate modelling, scenario generation, and reporting, raising the speed and sophistication of decision support across the function. Build scalable, self-serve analytics tools that give Finance, Pricing, Sales Ops, and business unit leaders consistent, decision-ready intelligence. Pricing & Monetization Analytics. Evaluate pricing changes through quantitative modelling of customer, revenue, and margin impact across segments and geographies. Track pricing and monetization KPIs (discount compliance, revenue realization, contribution margin) against targets, and quantify the financial impact of commercial governance decisions including pricing policies, discount frameworks, and packaging structures. Executive & Profitability Reporting. Deliver regular profitability and commercial performance reporting to ELT and GTM leadership, including a measurement framework that tracks strategic initiative effectiveness, monetization outcomes, and contribution margin across products, segments, and geographies. Partner with FP&A and Sales Ops to integrate pricing and profitability analytics into the forecast and planning cycle, and with Revenue Assurance and Finance Ops to remediate pricing-related revenue risks. Stakeholder Engagement & Decision Support. Act as the primary analytical partner to Pricing, Sales Enablement, and business unit leaders on profitability decisions, translating complex analysis into clear, actionable recommendations. Present findings, models, and recommendations to senior leadership in executive-ready format, and contribute to Board and investor materials covering pricing strategy, monetization performance, and platform progress. Required Skills & Qualifications:: University degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or a related quantitative field 5–7 years in financial analysis, FP&A, or quantitative/strategic finance in a SaaS or technology environment. Exceptional financial modelling and scenario-analysis skills, with a demonstrated track record building revenue, profitability, or pricing models and translating them into decision support (the core qualification for the role). Hands-on experience applying AI/ML tools (including LLMs and predictive modelling) to accelerate and modernize modelling and reporting workflows — a defining attribute of the role, not a nice-to-have. Preferred Skills & Qualifications:: Pricing or monetization experience (an asset, not a requirement) Experience with BI tools (Power BI preferred) and executive-grade data visualization. Build and maintain an agentic harness that enables users to query data and generate dashboards through natural language (an internal analog to agentic analysis tools such as Claude Cowork for our data). Partner with data platform, engineering, and Life Sciences stakeholders to translate business use cases into technical requirements and analysis-ready data products. Contribute to responsible AI practices, including appropriate handling and de-identification of sensitive healthcare data. Perform other job duties as assigned. Experience with clinical terminologies and coding systems (e.g., ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC) and with natural language processing on clinical or biomedical text. Familiarity with Life Sciences or Real-World Data / Real-World Evidence (RWD/RWE) use cases. Experience designing evaluation methodologies for AI/ML or LLM systems (accuracy metrics, annotation, error analysis). Proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience working within a modern data platform or cloud environment. Experience building data applications and pipelines. Job Description A bit about this role: We're looking for an experienced finance professional to take responsibility for the full cost picture across markets, products, segments, and legal entities. You will have the opportunity to work cross functionally with a wide group of internal stakeholders to ensure our planning, cost accounting and reporting give leadership a clear, trustworthy view of where our dollars go and why, so that we can deliver on our core values of treating every member as family. This opportunity is perfect for someone who is comfortable owning an allocation methodology and driver-based forecast model, and is able to draw the big picture from detailed analytics. You will not inherit a mature process, you will be shaping one. This role will report to our Director Financial Planning and Analysis. Your Responsibilities and Impact will include: Building and maintaining driver-based financial models that connect membership growth, staffing decisions, and vendor spend to the P&L and cash. Architect and scale the cost accounting framework, including expense allocation methodologies across all business segments and legal entities. Building business cases and ROI analyses, vendor and build-versus-buy decisions, market expansion and headcount investment, and then holding those investments accountable to what was modeled. Deliver market and product-level profitability analysis to guide leadership on margin optimization. Direct cost accounting policies, controls, and reporting to drive financial and growth objectives. Supporting the financial mechanics of intercompany arrangements, including cost allocation, transfer pricing inputs, and reporting requested by internal and third-party counterparties. Supporting or owning aspects of the monthly close related to cost, including accruals, allocations, variance analysis against budget and forecast, and management reporting packages that lead with drivers rather than restated numbers. Being an integral part of a cross-functional team focused on continuous improvement and standardization of policy, process and control, with a heavy emphasis on technology development and shifting our reporting out of spreadsheets and into scalable, self-service tooling. Supporting our market, network, and clinical teams with the education, tools, analysis, and supplemental reporting they need to manage their own cost performance. Ownership and responsibility for satisfying applicable audit, examination and other regulatory or compliance related inquiries and requests. Required skills and experience: A minimum of 5–10 years of finance and/or accounting experience. Demonstrated hands-on cost accounting experience including allocation methodology, cost center design, unit cost or product-level costing, and the discipline to defend how a number was built. Core FP&A or accounting experience: cost accounting, budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, variance analysis, and management reporting. Advanced financial modeling skills, including comfort working with large and imperfect data sets, AI, and/or a BI platform Deep understanding of ERP or planning systems, or in standing up a cost allocation model from scratch. The ability to explain financial results clearly to people who do not work in finance, and to challenge assumptions respectfully when the numbers do not support the story. The ability to thrive in a fast-paced, startup environment where priorities shift and process is something you help build. Desired skills and experience: Healthcare services and/or health insurance experience (preferred). An undergraduate and/or graduate degree in accounting, finance, business, or a related field. Job Description A bit about this role: Devoted Health engages in millions of member interactions every year through a frontline organization of team members and AI agents spanning Member Service, Specialty Care Coordination, and Member Outreach, Sales and more. The quality of those interactions is the mission. Every call, every outreach, every touchpoint is a moment where we either earn or lose a member's trust. Getting this right at scale requires a fundamentally new approach. You will build AI systems that monitor the quality of every member interaction and turn those signals into coaching and feedback that elevates both frontline team performance and frontline AI agent performance. You will define what high performance looks like across these teams and AI agents and build the systems that ensure we hit our goals. You will be a close thought partner to the leaders of our frontline teams, ensuring that every tool you build is adopted and helps them meaningfully improve performance. This is a new role, and you will shape what AI-native quality and performance operations looks like for this organization. Your Responsibilities and Impact will include: Embed with frontline teams and their leaders to understand what quality looks like in practice: how members are engaged, where interactions break down, and how coaching happens (or doesn't) today. Own the performance of our highest volume frontline AI agents, across voice and chat, and continue to build out those agents to drive higher performance. Build AI-powered quality monitoring systems that move the needle on our most important business outcomes. Evaluate member interactions in real time across millions of touchpoints, moving beyond pass/fail scoring to nuanced assessment of what actually matters for member experience, safety, and outcomes. Build coaching workflows that surface actionable feedback to leaders at all levels immediately, making every interaction an opportunity to improve. Every key stakeholder should have an approach to action on results so that we’re getting better every day. Visualize interaction data, evaluation criteria, coaching signals, and performance trends so the right insight reaches the right person at the right time, from rep to team lead to senior leader. Scale what works. Turn successful systems into reusable frameworks that extend to new teams, interaction types, and channels. What works for Member Service should accelerate what you build for Specialty Care Coordination, Member Outreach, and our Clinician orgs. Partner closely with frontline team leaders across levels, coaching them on how to use the tools you build, ensuring adoption, and iterating in real time in response to their feedback to drive value. Oversee a small team of operators and agent builders that will drive performance across all frontline agents and teams Required skills and experience: 4+ years in high-ownership operator roles: startup strategy, biz ops, consulting, or internal tooling PM. You have built and run systems that made organizations meaningfully more effective, and you move quickly to working prototypes on real data with real feedback. People leadership experience: you have directly managed, mentored, or grown individuals or teams, and you bring that lens to every cross-functional partnership. You know how to build trust quickly, give feedback that lands, and create the conditions for people around you to do their best work. Fluency with modern AI tools and platforms, with an active practice of pushing their limits. You're adaptive and curious — willing to learn, teach, lead, and follow. Strong data fluency: You self-serve analysis and reason from data rigorously: you know which numbers actually drive the business, can spot when a metric is misleading, and turn ambiguous data into clear insights on quality. Systems thinking: you move from solving a single issue to designing a framework that prevents an entire category of issues. You generalize your work and think in feedback loops, not isolated fixes. An instinct for quality in human interactions: you translate intuition about what a good member experience feels like into structured criteria an AI system can apply at scale. You care deeply about doing what's right for members and the teams serving them. A coaching and enabling mindset: you work with frontline managers and quality leads to ensure AI-generated insights actually change behavior. You challenge assumptions, do what makes sense even when it's unconventional, and care more about outcomes than credit. Exceptional communication: you tailor your style to move teams to action, from frontline guides to executives. You're comfortable with ambiguity and take ownership of outcomes end to end. Job Description A bit about this role: We can’t transform health care for America’s seniors alone. It requires coordination and information exchange within the healthcare supply chain. If we do it well, we believe we can improve how healthcare is paid for, delivered, and experienced. Having member clinical data is critical for understanding member healthcare needs to drive their health outcomes. The Clinical Data Acquisition Team ensures that clinical data is available at the right place and the right time for the Devoted teams. Your Responsibilities and Impact will include: Develop deep understanding of the clinical data needs (e.g. medical records, lab results, ADT, etc.) and data usability requirements across Devoted Health Plans and Devoted Medical. Collaborate with and align on outcomes with stakeholders across a variety of external partners and internal teams including Network Management, Risk Adjustment, Stars, Devoted Medical (Clinical teams), Payment Integrity, and others. Analyze clinical data availability across geographical areas to develop insights about data gaps, the reasons data is not available, and opportunities to obtain data. Using data insights, define an execution plan to ensure the broadest coverage of clinical data in the markets and ensure clinical data is usable by stakeholder teams. Implement technical integrations with Health Information Exchanges (HIEs), Labs, Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, data aggregators and other sources of clinical data and ensure quality of data received. Understand industry dynamics in order to explore new frameworks, optimize connections, and evaluate new or existing vendor relationships to scale data exchange, improve data quality, and minimize problematic data gaps. Explore and apply new processes and methodologies using AI to ensure clinical data is consistently available and usable by key stakeholders. Define, implement, and drive appropriate KPIs to measure success. Required skills and experience: 5+ years of experience in healthcare, healthcare technology, data operations, and/or program management, with demonstrated success leading complex initiatives or teams. Working knowledge of healthcare IT systems and data exchange methods, including SFTP, RESTful APIs, HL7 v2, and XML. Understanding of the healthcare interoperability landscape, including CMS interoperability requirements, FHIR, USCDI, TEFCA, and various EHR systems. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex data, identify insights, and translate findings into clear execution plans. Proficiency with SQL and Google Sheets or Excel for data analysis and reporting; familiarity with AI-powered productivity tools. Experience with Looker, Snowflake and GitHub is a plus. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to collaborate across Operations, Network Management, Product, and Technology and build effective relationships with external partners and executive stakeholders. Highly organized and results-oriented, with the ability to prioritize competing demands, manage critical work independently, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment to drive projects (such as a vendor implementation or stakeholder data investigation) to completion. Job Description This role is fully remote and must be located within one of the contiguous 50 states. You must be able and willing to work 3x12s or 4x10s as long as Saturday and Sunday are covered. A bit about this role: The Digital Care Program and the Responsive Care Department are redefining how we connect with patients by delivering exceptional clinical care entirely through chat and other digital channels. Our mission is to meet patients where they are — online, in real time, and with the same compassion, expertise, and partnership they would expect in person. As an Advanced Practice Provider (NP or PA) focused on Digital Care, you will be a cornerstone of this mission. You’ll provide holistic, empathetic care to patients across multiple geographies, leveraging your clinical expertise and keen attention to detail to ensure their needs are understood and addressed. Digital Care APPs are not just providers; they are trusted partners, guiding patients through symptom management, chronic disease care, medication review, and coordination across their broader healthcare teams within and outside of Devoted — all within a digital-first experience. This role requires the agility to respond to real-time patient demand, manage evolving digital workflows, and flex across Responsive Care programs while maintaining exceptional clinical quality, safety, and patient experience. What Makes a Digital NP at Devoted Special: You are unmatched in clinical expertise, yet every interaction is guided by empathy and partnership. You anticipate patient needs, solve problems proactively, and go above and beyond at every step. You treat every patient as a whole person, considering both clinical and personal priorities. You are an expert in service, turning digital touchpoints into meaningful, human-centered care experiences. Required skills and experience: APP with three or more years working with experience in primary care, house calls, internal medicine, family medicine, geriatrics, palliative care and/or urgent care. Ability to review AI-generated responses for clinical accuracy and safety. Licensure and certification For Nurse Practitioners: active and in-good-standing RN and APRN licenses. For Physician Assistants: an active and in-good-standing Physician Assistant license. Role licensure and certification in good standing is required and the ability to get licensed in requested states within 90 days of hire date, starting at offer letter signing. You will be required to get licensed in additional states as needed. We believe in making it easy for you to focus on patient care. Devoted Health will cover all costs and provide full administrative support for obtaining and maintaining licenses in all required states. Desired skills and experience: Prior virtual care or telehealth experience preferred, with passion for engaging patients digitally. Experience working in real-time, queue-based, or high-volume telehealth clinical environments. Experience collaborating with interdisciplinary care teams and coordinating care remotely. Comfort managing complex or vulnerable patient populations in a digital-first setting. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment with flexibility and curiosity. Responsibilities and Impact will include: Deliver exceptional, empathetic clinical care through real-time and asynchronous chat and other responsive care channels, supporting both the digital patient population and evolving queue-based needs across Responsive Care Department and the broader organization. Manage multiple concurrent and asynchronous patient conversations while maintaining clinical accuracy, timely documentation, and reliable follow-through. Guide and oversee patients’ medical management using a holistic framework (including the 5M approach: Mind, Mobility, Medications, Multicomplexity, Matters Most). Collaborate closely with patients’ primary care providers, specialists, and other teams such as pharmacy and specialty care to ensure continuity and comprehensiveness of care. Support patients’ care coordination with their family members and caregivers when appropriate, ensuring alignment with the patient’s priorities and goals. Provide thorough assessment, clinical guidance, and follow-up in response to patient-reported symptoms, medication questions, lab results, or new health concerns. Recognize when a patient’s needs cannot be safely or effectively addressed through chat and facilitate escalation to telephone, video, in-person, urgent, or emergency care as appropriate. Maintain ownership of patient needs through resolution or a clear, documented handoff. Maintain meticulous, accurate, and timely digital documentation in the electronic health record (EHR) in compliance with legal, ethical, and telehealth regulations. Continuously identify opportunities to improve patient experience and outcomes, leveraging digital workflows and proactive communication. Contribute to the improvement of digital workflows, standardized responses, escalation pathways, and quality standards. Occasionally support broader Devoted Medical service lines in line with program growth and team needs. Provide flexible clinical coverage across Responsive Care Department queues and on-call services as patient demand and operational priorities evolve. Adhere to all relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards, including patient privacy and telehealth regulations. Automate operational toil so the platform stays fast to build on as it scales. Job Description: Cityblock is putting AI directly into the hands of the care teams and members we serve. You are a full-stack product engineer who takes an AI-native idea from a rough prototype to a feature running in production, in front of real clinical users, and you contribute to the prototyping loop that lets product and design move at that speed. Most of the value of AI in our product is still undiscovered. Your job is to shorten the distance between an idea and something people can actually use, and then to productionize effective use of AI into features that hold up in a regulated healthcare product. Reporting into the Product Engineering org, this role covers system design, including the LLM/SDK integration underneath, the evals and golden datasets that tell you whether it's working, and the UX. You embed with product, design, and work with clinical operations. Because these features run in a regulated healthcare product in front of real members and care teams, you help decide where AI acts on its own, where it stays advisory with a human in the loop, and how we prove a feature is safe to trust, designing for compliance from the start. Responsibilities Implement full-stack feature work that integrates LLM APIs and SDKs into member- and care-team-facing product surfaces. Own features end to end: system design, model/SDK integration, evals, and the UX that determines whether the feature is actually trusted and used. Build observability and evals alongside the feature, so quality can be measured and then improved. Apply and help improve the team's prototyping loop, eval discipline, and quality bar through the work you ship. Put prototypes in front of real users early, learn from what breaks, and harden the ones worth keeping into production. Bring an honest read of what's feasible back to product and design, so the roadmap reflects reality. Work with product management, design, and clinical operations to find and understand the high-value AI opportunities behind the features you build. Partner with the data organization for the grounded, trustworthy context your features depend on. Requirements for the Role 4+ years of experience as an engineer You are a strong full-stack product engineer who ships. You solve problems by building working software. Experience integrating LLM APIs or SDKs into a shipped product, or closely related production experience you can build on. Strong product sense: you care about whether people use your products and whether they provide measurable value. Comfort owning ambiguity by taking a well-scoped, high-value idea and turning it into something real, with decreasing guidance over time. Experience building evals or quality measurement for AI features, or the clear instinct that you need to. Fluent daily use of AI assistants for engineering, with a clear sense of when to trust them and when not to. Drawn to mission-oriented work, and comfortable partnering with clinical and design experts whose expertise differs from yours. Nice to Have A CS degree or equivalent. Prior work in a regulated or compliance-heavy environment (HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar). Experience building AI-native product features from scratch, including the evals around them. Design sensibility strong enough to prototype UX yourself. Exposure to clinical operations or working alongside clinical staff as end users. Hands-on with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): embeddings, vector search, and grounding LLM output in trusted context. Familiarity with agentic patterns including tool/function calling, structured outputs, and multi-step orchestration. Experience with LLM eval and observability tooling (e.g., Braintrust, LangSmith) and LLM-as-judge techniques. Comfort in a modern TypeScript/Node/React stack, including streaming and latency-sensitive LLM UX. Responsibilities: Provide data management, manipulation, cleaning, and analysis support for biomedical aging research projects, including the validation and benchmarking of epigenetic clocks and other aging biomarkers across harmonized, multi-dataset resources. Participate as a team member in development of algorithms and software tools, including data harmonization pipelines and exploration of AI-agent and foundation-model methods, facilitating scientific productivity and project completion. Job Summary The Director of Research Computing, Data & Technology reports to the Vice President, Administration and Finance at the Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute (Institute), a research and teaching partnership between Point32Health and Harvard Medical School. Job Summary Reporting to the Director of Risk Adjustment Reporting and Analytics, the Manager of Reporting and Analytics – Medicare Advantage will apply a blend of advanced business, analytical, technical, and leadership skills to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of risk adjustment data submissions to CMS. This role will optimize risk score accuracy, support revenue performance across all Medicare Advantage products, and ensure the timely, accurate, and compliant submission and reporting of All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) files to six state agencies. This individual will synthesize large data sets, complex information and work effectively across business areas including Member Operations, Provider Information, Claims, Information Technology (IT) and Actuarial. The Manager will possess a strong understanding of data architecture, data lineage, and relational databases and will actively partner with IT teams on solution design, data flow analysis, root-cause investigations, implementation planning, and quality assurance of IT deliverables. The Manager will lead a team of 3-4 senior analysts and data leads, providing coaching, mentorship, performance management, and professional development to build a highly engaged and high-performing team. In addition, the Manager will oversee all EDS/EDPS submissions for Point32Health and serve as the organization's subject matter expert for Medicare Advantage Encounter Data Processing System (EDS/EDPS) submissions and APCD reporting. Job Description Key Responsibilities/Duties – what you will be doing (top five): 1. Medicare Advantage and APCD Data Governance, Reporting, and Submission Oversight: Be responsible for the planning, execution, program implementation, and monitoring of Medicare Advantage and All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) data submission and reporting efforts. Regularly review the effectiveness, accuracy, and compliance of claims, supplemental data, and APCD submission processes, infrastructure, and reporting; recommend design enhancements and implement changes as needed. Oversee the maintenance of data controls, dashboard reporting, and routine data reconciliations, and provide regular updates to management. Routinely present key issues, business updates, and performance metrics related to Medicare Advantage risk adjustment. 2. Collaboration and Stakeholder Management: Collaborate closely with Actuarial on Medicare Advantage analytics, program, and provider-level analyses, and targeting. Partner with internal stakeholders, including Claims, Membership Operations, Provider Information, External Vendors, and IT, to ensure that process enhancements and data management mechanisms are developed, maintained, and monitored on an ongoing basis. Lead communication, coordination, issue resolution, and compliance-related activities with six state agencies related to All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) submissions, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant reporting. Participate in and contribute to strategic planning efforts and annual risk adjustment business plan development. Participate in CMS and industry calls and monitor changes in regulations and technical specifications affecting EDS/EDPS and APCD submissions. Serve as the organization's subject matter expert for EDS/EDPS (Encounter Data Processing System) and APCD reporting requirements, both internally and in interactions with CMS and state regulatory agencies. 3. Data Optimization, Submissions, and Integrity: Oversee data management and submission responsibilities for EDS/EDPS CMS submissions for Massachusetts HMO, PPO, SCO, Unify products and Connecticut HMO and PPO products, as well as All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) submissions to six state agencies. Ensure timely, complete, accurate, and compliant data submissions and reporting. Review CMS-reported errors, outliers, and data quality findings, and collaborate with Actuarial, IT, Operational, and vendor partners to remediate issues, implement corrective actions, or provide appropriate justification. Coordinate all required reviews and sign-offs for EDS/EDPS and APCD submissions. Develop internal capabilities and/or partner with vendors to support data optimization efforts, maintaining a catalog of data quality, operational efficiency, and submission enhancement opportunities. Participate, as required, in corporate project and strategic initiatives, including the development, evaluation, and presentation of business cases related to EDS/EDPS, APCD, and data optimization efforts. Oversee and monitor the processes for accepting, submitting, reconciling, and accurately tracking all supplemental submissions and deletes. Review and assess CMS HPMS memoranda and related regulatory guidance, identify operational and reporting impacts, and partner with internal stakeholders to ensure timely implementation of required actions, process changes, and compliance obligations 4. Analytics and Reporting: Coordinate with vendors and/or Actuarial teams to ensure that accurate and complete data is utilized for valuation, forecasting, targeting, and performance analyses supporting Medicare Advantage products. Manage and perform data analytics to support ongoing and emerging risk adjustment initiatives. Build, maintain, and enhance EDS/EDPS tieback processes and reporting for actuarial valuation exercises. Job Summary Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute is currently seeking a highly motivated individual to join our organization as SAS Programmer, who will work collaboratively with investigators, statisticians, and senior programmers. The SAS Programmer will work within the Division of Health Policy and Insurance Research (HPI) within the Department of Population Medicine (DPM). The SAS Programmer will perform a variety of activities to support the project team, including assisting with data cleaning, database development, dataset creation, software programming, data management, statistical analysis, and results reporting for internal and external research projects. The individual will primarily work with large health insurance claims data (e.g., CMS Medicaid claims data, All Payer Claims Data) under the direction of a senior programmer and project manager. The SAS programmer will work across a multi-project research portfolio examining effects of health policies on health outcomes, including work focused on maternal health, child health, and mental health. Their work will be done in collaboration with the larger research team, which includes health services researchers, biostatisticians, clinicians, economists, and epidemiologists. WHO WE ARE The Department of Population Medicine (DPM) is a research and teaching collaboration between Harvard Medical School (HMS) and Harvard Pilgrim Health Care. Our mission is to improve health care delivery and population health through research and education, in partnership with health plans, delivery systems, and public health agencies. As the nation’s first medical school appointing department based in a health plan, we are strategically positioned to improve population health and health care delivery locally, nationally, and internationally. DPM is home to five divisions and six Centers of Excellence, which facilitate collaborations across divisions. Researchers in DPM work closely with other Harvard faculty at HMS, at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, and across the University, as well as many health systems, hospitals, and community partners. The Division of Health Policy and Insurance Research (HPI) is one of five divisions within DPM. Our researchers study state and federal policies, payment and insurance reforms, care delivery models, and digital health innovations – with a focus on both commercial (employer sponsored insurance, Marketplace) and public (Medicaid, Medicare) populations and payers – in core areas of: pharmaceutical policy and systems, maternal and child health, mental health and substance use, chronic disease, cancer, and health care workforce. We do so using quasi-experimental and other health services research methods, with large administrative data sources (claims data, EHR data, survey data), with an overarching focus on access, quality, affordability, and equity of care for marginalized populations. We work in close collaboration with local, national, and international partners. WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING • Use SAS software to clean, quality check, and troubleshoot health insurance claims data • Design, develop, test, execute, and maintain SAS programs to create cohorts and generate variables • Create and maintain analytic datasets using raw data files, including complex data linkages, merging, and transformation workflows • Generate descriptive data and conduct statistical analyses, in close consultation with investigators, statisticians, and senior programmers • Use Excel or other programs to display user-friendly results in graphical or numerical form • Utilize knowledge of analytic and statistical concepts, techniques, and methods in daily work • Participate in project meetings, both via telephone and in-person • Contribute to the development of manuscripts and reports • Perform out-of-the-box thinking, collaborate with others, and make a difference every day! QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED • Bachelor’s Degree (BA, BS) • At least 2 years of full-time work as a programmer or equivalent SAS programming experience, including macro programming and PROC SQL • Experience transforming and analyzing large administrative health care data, including claims data (such as CMS Medicaid or Medicare claims, all-payer claims databases, commercial claims) • Experience with epidemiologic and biostatistics principles and methods • Ability to prioritize work, operate under tight deadlines, and meet deadlines • Proficiency with software packages, including Microsoft Office suite (e.g., Excel) • Excellent organizational skills, accuracy, and attention to detail. • Resilient, collaborative, flexible, and independent PREFERRED • Master's Degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Statistics, or another health-related field • Programming experience in at least one other programming language (e.g., Stata, R) • Knowledge of health care systems, health care delivery, or health policy • Experience with, and understanding of, claims-related elements such as ICD diagnosis codes and procedure codes • Experience conducting regression analyses WHAT MAKES US STAND OUT • Work-Life-Flexibility • Paid volunteer time off (up to 3 days annually) • Open Time Off • Annual Mini-Grant of $500 donated to a non-profit organization of the employee’s choice • Educational Reimbursement WORKING ENVIRONMENT Hybrid office environment based in Boston, MA. All faculty and staff are expected to be in the office on Thursdays. Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders. This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud. As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1. Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions. Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact. Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders. Success in this role looks like: In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals. By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt. Employment Type: Full time Shift: Description: Analyst, Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible for creation and production of timely and accurate performance analytics across multiple segments and for various levels of the organization, supporting financial planning and forecasting processes, developing insightful modeling/decision support data, identifying financial trends and opportunities, monitoring variances and root causes, and recommending appropriate improvement actions. Job Summary The Senior Analyst, Financial Planning & Analysis is responsible for leading a broad array of analytical, consultative, and financial management functions across multiple business processes, organizational segments and consolidation points. This role leverages data, reporting tools, and financial models to identify trends, analyze variances, uncover opportunities, and provide actionable insights to leadership. Responsibilities include timely and accurate financial planning and forecasting, administration of workforce analytic systems, proforma/scenario modeling, identifying and managing financial trends and opportunities along with driving improvement in partnership with operational and financial leadership. Key Qualifications: Experience with database management and SQL Server. Proficiency in Tableau, Business Objects, or similar BI/reporting tools. Strong analytical, data visualization, and financial modeling skills. Ability to manage large datasets and translate complex data into business insights. Experience automating reporting and improving data-driven decision processes. Experience with Workday, UKG, Oracle Planning/Capital and/or Freeform also a plus. Employment Type: Part time Shift: Rotating Shift Description: MED LAB SCIENTIST / CLINICAL LAB SCIENTIST NAMPA SOUTH LAB PRN SUMMARY: Performs tests related to the diagnosis and treatment of patient by utilizing various medical laboratory procedures in the Clinical Laboratory. Correlates and integrates other patient data when interpreting test results. Uses professional judgment and has an in-depth knowledge of laboratory techniques, scientific principles, quality control, and instrument maintenance. Recognizes problems, identifies causes, and determines alternative methods and solutions. REQUIREMENTS: Bachelor's Degree Required. Medical Technologist (MT), Medical Laboratory Scientist (MLS), Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) or equivalent certification by the American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) or American Medical Technologist (AMT) required or registry eligible and obtained within 1 year of hire date. Completion of medical technology training required. WHAT YOU WILL DO: You will have the opportunity to rotate in Chemistry, Blood Bank, Heme/Coag, Micro and Speciality Chemistry. Performs, records and reviews scheduled QC. Takes immediate corrective action when QC data is outside established limits. Performs and records routine maintenance of equipment. Recognizes and documents poor instrument performance and takes appropriate action independently. Verifies specimen labeling, integrity and suitability before performing testing. Accurately performs low, medium and high complexity testing procedures according to established protocols and regulatory requirements. Reports test results accurately and appropriately. Reports critical test results to physician, nursing station or physician office according to established protocol. Ability to prioritize work to maintain maximum efficiency. Uses spare time to assist other areas as needed. Perform phlebotomy when needed according to laboratory policies and procedures. Monitors supply inventory and take appropriate action to ensure that needed supplies are readily available. Reviews work performed by clinical laboratory assistants. Perform corrective actions if required. Performs expected tasks without direction of supervisor. Ensures accuracy of work being reported by assigned department. Examine review lists, pending logs and the like. Resolves problems immediately and communicates with oncoming shift, nurses/physicians as appropriate. Employment Type: Full time Shift: Description: *Hybrid Position- 3 days a week in office *Must live near Trinity Location Purpose Health Informatics (HI) is the specialty that integrates health care science, computer science, and information science to manage and communicate data, information, knowledge and wisdom in clinical practice across the care continuum. Health informatics facilitates the integration of data, information, knowledge and wisdom to support operations. This support is accomplished with information structures, information processes, and information technology. The goal of informatics is to improve the health of populations, communities, families, and individuals by optimizing information management and communication. These activities include the design and use of informatics solutions and technology to support all areas of health care delivery, including, but not limited to, the direct provision of care, establishing effective administrative systems, managing and delivering education experiences, enhancing lifelong learning, and supporting health care research. Essential Functions Our Trinity Health Culture: Knows, understands, incorporates & demonstrates our Trinity Health Mission, Values, Vision, Actions & Promise in behaviors, practices & decisions. Work Focus: Researches, collects & analyzes information. Identifies opportunities, develops solutions, & leads through resolution. Collaborates on performance improvement activities as indicated by outcomes in program efficiency & patient experience. Responsible for distribution of analytical reports. Process Focus: Utilizes multiple system applications to perform analysis, create reports & develop educational materials. Incorporates basic knowledge of TH policies, practices & processes to ensure quality, confidentiality, & safety are prioritized. Demonstrates knowledge of departmental processes & procedures & ability to readily acquire new knowledge. Data Management & Analysis: Research & compiles information to support ad-hoc operational projects & initiatives. Synthesizes & analyzes data & provides detailed summaries including graphical data presentations illustrating trends & recommending practical options or solutions while considering the impact on business strategy & supporting leadership decision making. Leverages program & operational data & measurements to define & demonstrate progress, ROI & impacts. Maintains a working knowledge of applicable Federal, state & local laws/regulations, Trinity Health Integrity & Compliance Program & Code of Conduct, as well as other policies, procedures & guidelines in order to ensure adherence in a manner that reflects safe, honest, ethical & professional behavior & safe work practices. Minimum Qualifications Must possess a comprehensive knowledge of Health Informatics through a combination of education and experience. Must possess a working knowledge of Health Informatics with at least two (2) years of experience in an informatics or related role and experience with clinical information systems and health information technology. Basic understanding of clinical treatment modalities, educational principles, clinical information systems, accreditation and regulatory standards, and program development. Demonstrated knowledge and application of change management principles. Demonstrated knowledge and application of project management principles. Additional Qualifications (nice to have) Certification from a national informatics certifying body preferred. Fellowship, academic courses, or other formal training in Health Informatics preferred. Bachelors Degree with the focus on Health Informatics or related discipline preferred OR equivalent combination of education and experience. Physical & Mental Requirements & Working Conditions Indirect / Healthcare Support Services: (OSHA: Healthcare support services mean services that facilitate the provision of healthcare services.) · Occasional clinical / patient facing work environment. · Includes continuous work time indoors (subject to travel requirements) under temperature-controlled & well-lit conditions; may encounter occasional variable external environmental conditions. · Includes occasional lifting, up to 30 pounds unassisted, frequent travel & use of computer; Includes continuous sitting & may require occasional long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, bending, pulling & pushing. Direct Healthcare & Indirect / Support Healthcare Services: must be able to: · Adapt to frequent interruptions, shifting priorities & stressful situations; Attend to tasks until complete, understand & relate to complex ideas & concepts & be able to remember multiple tasks & regimens extending over long periods of time & work on concurrent tasks / projects. · Continuously Read small print, frequent ability to hear normal sounds & voice patterns, able to give / receive instructions & other verbal communications in-person & over the phone / computer / device / equipment assigned with some background noise. · Perform frequent manual dexterity activities & occasional grasping/handling. · Continuous attention to maintain a safe working environment & use of available personal protective equipment (PPE). ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS Knows, understands, incorporates, and demonstrates the Trinity Health Mission, Vision, and Values in leadership behaviors, practices, supports and endorses senior leadership decisions, goals, objectives, and strategies. Provides a work environment that fosters positive energy, creativity, and teamwork among associates across all functional areas. Provides consultative, operational, and technical support to RHM technicians, and RHM leadership in support of medical equipment capital planning, safety, hazard alerts/recalls, and asset management. Ensures short and long-term regional financial objectives stay on course and drives initiatives with RHM teams that contribute to Trinity UEM and THCE program short and long-term operational excellence. Presents findings and recommendations to the Regional Director or Senior Manager to be used in strategic planning and other key decisions. Obtains final approval from Regional Director or Senior Manager prior to implementing program changes to the RHM. Identifies, recommends, and implements best practices and operational solutions to improve CE service delivery at the RHM. Works with Contract Manager to ensure vendor service agreements provide expected service value, are necessity, accurately reflect accepted terms and conditions, and align with future service strategy. Takes necessary steps to minimize reliance on outside vendor service support. Reviews subsequent FY goals/objectives and related strategic plans as defined by the senior leadership team (SLT); outlines expectations, accountabilities, and measurables used in determining success. Reviews Customer Satisfaction Survey scores for discrepancies and overall customer satisfaction. Prepares Performance Improvement Plans (PIP) where necessary to resolve customer satisfaction issues and address Program Quality Evaluation (PQE) deficiencies. Interviews, hires, trains, appraises, counsels, and supervises technical and support staff; handles disciplinary actions. Reviews and approves expense reports and holds direct reports accountable to Trinity Health and THCE policies and procedures. Prepares hiring justifications to ensure financial cost saving merit. Prepares Return-On-Investment (ROI) analysis, ensures projected targets are achieved and reviews results with Regional Director. Ensures timely completion of annual performance appraisals; addresses associate problems and issues related to their work or environment. Fosters the development of diverse teams at both administrative and technical levels and outlines annual skills development, career growth opportunities, and improvement objectives with direct reports. Establishes and monitors progress on objectives and takes the necessary actions to resolve and prevent recurring issues. Provides the necessary leadership and oversight in cases where disciplinary action or termination is warranted. Reviews and monitors short and long-term regional financial plans and objectives. Measures successes and deficiencies and recommends any corrective course of action and monitors implementation and compliance assessment. Approves purchases within established scope and authority. Experience in medical equipment service management, project management, and implementing best practices in a service support group, leading cross-functional work teams, with demonstrated results in reducing medical equipment repair and service costs. Ability to work effectively in a diverse, collaborative, and team oriented culture. Ability to develop methodologies for collecting and analyzing relevant data; to audit CE program processes; monitor quality; identify, problems and their root causes, and make recommendations for improvement. Excellent leadership, analytical, organizational, planning, delegation, coaching, communication (verbal, written and interpersonal), and computer (MS Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) skills with a continuous improvement mindset. A personal presence characterized by a sense of honesty, integrity, and caring with the ability to inspire and motivate others to promote the philosophy, mission, vision, goals, and values of Trinity Health. Schedule : Full-Time, 40 Hours- Day Shift Position Purpose: Position performs a variety of duties in and around the buildings of the Hospital complex in an effort to maintain Plant Operations 24/7. Duties include repairs, monitoring and reporting problems with machinery, systems and mechanical equipment, heating, ventilation equipment, air conditioning, refrigeration systems, kitchen equipment, Building Management Systems, and Fire Alarm Systems. Employment Type: Full time Shift: Day Shift Description: GENERAL SUMMARY AND PURPOSE: The Regional Life Safety Engineer provides system-wide inspection of rated assemblies and corrective maintenance of those assemblies. By evaluating existing conditions, interpreting Life Safety Code requirements, identifying compliance risks, and implementing practical solutions that support patient safety, operational continuity, and accreditation readiness. Working on a team of two Engineers based in Boise , the Regional Life Safety Engineer will spend time going to each of our four hospital locations (Boise, Nampa, Ontario, and Baker City), inspecting and working with facility personnel on any changes/improvements needed. The Regional Life Safety Engineer applies advanced technical knowledge, sound professional judgment, and a collaborative approach to assist engineering leadership in maintaining compliance with applicable codes, standards, and accreditation requirements. The position serves as a trusted technical resource to Engineering, Safety, Infection Prevention, Planning, Design and Construction, Clinical Operations, and executive leadership. SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: High school diploma or equivalent required. Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare facilities, commercial facilities, construction, building engineering, code compliance, fire protection, or a closely related technical field. Valid driver's license with the ability to travel routinely throughout Idaho and Oregon. Demonstrated ability to read and interpret architectural drawings, life safety plans, specifications, technical manuals, and regulatory requirements. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and communicate effectively with leaders, contractors, clinicians, and regulatory agencies. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Meets Health System's Guiding Behaviors and Caring Standards including interpersonal communication and professional conduct expectations. Provides leadership for the planning, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of the Saint Alphonsus Life Safety Compliance Program. Establishes inspection methodologies, documentation standards, performance expectations, and quality improvement initiatives. Coordinates annual inspection and correction activities. Monitors program performance and adjusts schedules to ensure timely completion. Creates performance indicators, dashboards, and written reports that communicate inspection completion rates, regulatory deficiencies, corrective action status, and emerging compliance risks. Performs detailed evaluations in accordance with NFPA 80, organizational policies, and applicable regulatory requirements. Identifies deficiencies and performs corrective actions that support patient safety and accreditation readiness. Evaluates fire-rated walls, floors, ceilings, shafts, smoke barriers, and other fire-resistance-rated assemblies to verify compliance with Life Safety Code requirements. Documents deficiencies and collaborates with facility personnel to preserve compartmentation and reduce organizational risk. Inspects above-ceiling spaces during maintenance and construction activities to verify the integrity of fire and smoke barriers, firestopping systems, and other life safety features. Coordinates corrective actions when deficiencies or unapproved penetrations are identified. Conducts systematic compliance assessments of healthcare occupancies, support buildings, and renovation projects. Develops, maintains, and continuously updates inspection reports, compliance databases, supporting documentation, and electronic records. Creates, prioritizes, performs and corrective work orders resulting from inspections, surveys, and compliance assessments. Provides technical guidance regarding corrective actions beyond the capability of the inspection team and monitors progress until identified deficiencies are satisfactorily resolved. Evaluates architectural drawings, life safety plans, and project documents to identify potential compliance concerns before construction begins. Assists project teams in evaluating construction-related risks and implementing Interim Life Safety Measures when required. Monitors compliance with approved ILSM plans and recommends adjustments as project conditions change. Serves as a technical resource for project managers, architects, contractors, and engineering leadership throughout planning, design, construction, and project closeout. Helps identify compliance risks early and recommends solutions that protect the healthcare environment while supporting successful project delivery. ABOUT THE JOB The ACLU seeks applicants for a full-time two-year fellowship position in the Speech, Privacy and Technology Project of the ACLU’s National office in New York, NY. ICF supports governments and organisations on challenges in areas such as energy, the environment, aviation, health and public policy. Confidence working independently and engaging stakeholders across teams, clear written and spoken English for technical and nontechnical audiences. ICF’s Fish and Aquatic Science and Technology Team is in an exciting period of expansion and invites applications for a Senior Data Scientist position. The Senior Data Scientist will work closely with fish biologists, hydrologists, and project managers to assist water resource clients with quantitative analysis, decision support modeling, and publication of applied science. Most immediate assignments will focus on statistical and decision support modeling and publishing work on Chinook Salmon in California’s Central Valley, though there will be opportunities for future work in other regions. The successful applicant will demonstrate the following: Fish Data Expertise with knowledge of and experience with key issues confronting fish management in Northern California, including Chinook Salmon population dynamics, endangered species recovery, habitat restoration, flow management, and monitoring program design. Water Management Expertise with knowledge of and experience with key issues confronting water management in California, including reservoir and conveyance operations, water supply and allocation, environmental flows, and drought and flood management. Ability to understand and interpret water operations, hydrologic and hydraulic information, and their implications for fish populations, habitat, and management decisions. Familiarity with California water policy and the legislative process. Quantitative and Problem-Solving Expertise: Knowledge and aptitude for quantitative analysis to evaluate the effects of clients’ proposed actions; ability to design and apply sophisticated, robust, and creative analytical approaches, including hierarchical and Bayesian statistical models and machine learning; ability to interpret hydrologic, hydraulic, and telemetry modeling outputs and integrate them into fish population and decision-support models; ability to conduct and interpret advanced statistical analyses; and proficiency in R, Python, and SQL. Excellent Verbal and Written Communication Skills: Peer-reviewed scientific publication record and experience presenting at professional conferences. Project Management Skills: Ability to manage several simultaneous long-term projects, including budget tracking, staff coordination, client relationship management, and completion of all required products/reports. Team Leadership Skills: Demonstrated track record of setting high personal performance and quality standards and enabling the team to be successful; viewing all team members as critical and treating team members with respect and professionalism; collaborating and leveraging team member strengths; and mentoring/developing junior team members, including through code review and documentation practices. Develop reusable MLOps and LLMOps patterns using Azure Databricks, Databricks ML, MLflow, Unity Catalog, Azure Machine Learning, Python, and approved Azure AI services. Integrate ML workflows with source control, infrastructure provisioning, secrets management, identity and access controls, environment management, and enterprise release processes. Create and maintain deployment templates, reusable repositories, operational runbooks, model documentation, release evidence, and technical standards that accelerate responsible AI/ML adoption across the enterprise. The Software Asset Management Product Owner - Enterprise SaaS functions as the product owner for a defined portfolio of enterprise SaaS applications (e.g., collaboration platforms, productivity tools, or designated enterprise SaaS systems). This role blends IT Asset Management (ITAM) disciplines—licensing, renewals, cost optimization, and compliance—with hands‑on application administration and engineering to ensure SaaS applications are secure, well‑integrated, and efficiently operated. As the technical steward for sanctioned SaaS tools, this role partners with Security, Identity, Procurement, Finance, and Enterprise Architects to ensure applications are securely onboarded, access is governed and auditable, and manual work is automated wherever possible, supporting modernization, security, and operational efficiency of the SaaS portfolio. Key Responsibilities 1. Product Ownership & Value Delivery ( ~ 35%) Own roadmap and backlog for assigned SaaS applications or ITAM tooling. Drive operational improvements through automation, standardized practices, and governance oversight. Balance compliance requirements with business productivity needs. Act as primary interface between business stakeholders and engineering/support teams. Define success metrics (adoption, cost efficiency, risk posture). Evaluate and vet new SaaS tools for technical compatibility, security posture, integration requirements, and administrative overhead prior to adoption. 2. Application Administration & Security Engineering (~35%) Serve as the technical application administrator for approved SaaS platforms, ensuring secure, scalable, and efficient day-to-day operations. Partner with Identity, Security, and other teams to configure and maintain: SSO and conditional access integrations MFA enforcement, admin role assignments, and security settings Automation workflows for SaaS administration, including license provisioning/deprovisioning, role assignments, and access reviews Implement and support least-privilege access models, including management of service accounts, service principals, secrets, and API permissions. Oversee and automate user lifecycle processes (joiner, mover, leaver), ensuring access provisioning aligns with role, policy, and audit requirements. Leverage AI, APIs, scripting, and low-code platforms to reduce manual administrative effort and improve operational consistency. Establish and document application administration standards, including admin ownership models, access review cadences, and secure configuration baselines. Act as an escalation point for complex application and access-related issues beyond Tier 1/2 support. 3. SaaS Financial & Lifecycle Management (~30%) Own the software lifecycle for defined portfolio of enterprise SaaS applications, from onboarding through renewal and retirement. Monitor application usage, license consumption, and spending to: Identify under‑utilization and seat reclamation opportunities Recommend license model changes and contract right‑sizing Lead renewal readiness by partnering with Finance and Procurement using historical usage and forward‑looking demand. Maintain a clean, authoritative SaaS inventory, including license entitlements, assigned users, admins, and integrations. Drive visibility and optimization of SaaS spend, utilization, and risk posture across the assigned portfolio. Support internal and external audits by performing periodic user access reviews and license compliance validations. Execute governance processes in alignment with ITAM program standards. Required Skills: 3+ years of experience in SaaS application administration, or IT Asset Management, with demonstrated hands-on technical depth. 3+ years of demonstrated experience configuring, securing, and integrating SaaS applications in an enterprise environment, including SSO, API connections, and admin console management. Strong understanding of software licensing models (named, concurrent, consumption, enterprise agreements). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect usage, entitlement, and spend data into actionable insights and recommendations. Ability to maintain accurate configuration and inventory data across multiple platforms, and to identify discrepancies through data analysis and system queries. Demonstrated initiative in adopting and applying emerging technologies, including AI and automation tooling, to streamline operations and improve decision-making. Desired Skills & Experience Working knowledge of: ITAM or SAM tooling CMDB or application inventory platforms Experience with: SSO technologies (SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect) Identity platforms (e.g., Entra ID / Azure AD) Familiarity with: Service principals, API permissions, Graph‑style access models SaaS security configurations and vendor admin consoles Experience automating workflows using scripting, APIs, Power Platform, or similar tools. Bachelor’s degree Experience building dashboards and reports (Excel and/or BI tools) and communicating results to non-technical stakeholders. Comfortable operating at the intersection of governance, engineering, and cost optimization. Hands on experience supporting SOX, ITGC, or access review processes. ICF is hiring a Senior Research Analyst to perform a critical role within the Office Child Labor, Forced Labor and Human Trafficking (OCFT) of the International Labor Affairs Bureau (ILAB) at the U.S. Department of Labor. ILAB increases American job and wage growth by combating foreign labor abuses and unfair trade practices in global supply chains that undermine U.S. prosperity and security. The position requires the ability to provide expert advice to ILAB regarding opportunities in global commerce to create and enforce labor standards for trade agreements to combat child labor, forced labor, and human trafficking in global supply chains that undermine the American economy and security. The Senior Research Analyst is a mid-level, non-supervisory position responsible for conducting complex, high-impact research in support of organizational priorities, statutory requirements, and congressionally mandated reporting. Working with a high degree of independence and analytical judgment, the analyst proactively identifies and executes research opportunities, evaluates complex qualitative and quantitative information, and develops findings and recommendations for senior leadership and other stakeholders. The position provides ILAB with expert research on governments’ efforts to eliminate exploitative labor from supply chains and the worst forms of child labor. The position also provides—in conjunction and under the supervision of OCFT leadership—mentorship, review, and guidance to junior analysts. The position reports to the ICF Senior Manager and at DOL the Lead International Relations Officers and/or Division Chiefs within OCFT and may be based in Washington, DC, or remotely. Key Responsibilities: Advanced Research and Analysis for Congressionally Mandated Reports: Conducts and supports research necessary to fulfill congressionally mandated reporting and other statutory or organizational requirements. Independently identifies and pursues research opportunities that strengthen, expand, or otherwise further the organization's ability to meet congressionally mandated reports, including the List of Goods Produced by Child Labor or Forced Labor and/or List of Products Produced by Forced or Indentured Child Labor . Independently determines appropriate research approaches, methodologies, data sources, and analytical techniques based on the nature and objectives of the research. Synthesizes information from multiple qualitative and quantitative sources to identify trends, relationships, risks, gaps, and emerging issues. Evaluates the reliability, relevance, and limitations of available information and applies sound analytical judgment when information is incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous. Develops well-supported findings, conclusions, and recommendations and clearly communicates the significance and implications of research results to technical and non-technical audiences. Anticipates emerging research needs and identifies opportunities to address information gaps, improve the evidence base for required reporting, and enhance the quality and relevance of organizational research products. Maintains awareness of relevant legislative, policy, programmatic, and research developments and assesses their potential implications for current and future analytical work. Guidance and Mentorship: Provides technical guidance and mentorship to junior research analysts by sharing research best practices, analytical methods, institutional knowledge, and subject-matter expertise. Reviews research and analytical products and provides substantive, constructive feedback to strengthen methodological rigor, accuracy, clarity, and analytical reasoning. Assists junior analysts—in conjunction and under the supervision of OCFT leadership—in addressing complex research questions, evaluating sources and evidence, interpreting findings, and effectively communicating analytical results. Research Products and Communication: Prepares or contributes to high-quality reports, briefings, memoranda, presentations, and other analytical products for senior leadership, congressional reporting, and other internal or external stakeholders. Translates complex research findings into clear, concise, and defensible conclusions tailored to the needs of the intended audience. Presents and explains research methodologies, findings, limitations, and implications and responds to substantive questions regarding analytical work. Quality Assurance and Research Improvement: Provides a senior-level review of analytical research products, as appropriate, to help ensure research is methodologically sound, appropriately supported by evidence, and consistent with applicable standards and requirements. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: The position requires advanced knowledge of research principles, methodologies, and analytical techniques; demonstrated ability to independently design and execute complex research projects; and skill in evaluating and synthesizing qualitative and quantitative information from diverse sources. The incumbent must demonstrate strong analytical judgment, critical thinking, written and oral communication, and the ability to develop defensible findings and recommendations from complex or incomplete information. The position also requires the ability to provide effective technical guidance and mentorship, coordinate analytical work across multiple contributors, and communicate complex findings to senior leaders and other stakeholders. The Senior Research Analyst must demonstrate initiative in identifying emerging research needs and opportunities, particularly those that support or strengthen congressionally mandated reporting and other high-priority organizational requirements. Required Qualifications: Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional research experience conducting complex research on international child labor, forced labor, exploitative labor practices, or global supply chains. Experience contributing to congressionally mandated, statutory, or other U.S. Government reports and research products. Demonstrated ability to independently identify, develop, and execute research projects addressing emerging issues or information gaps. Security Clearance: Ability to obtain low-level security clearance (U.S. citizenship, having resided in the U.S. for the past 2 years, and ability to perform the work of this position from a location within the United States). Preferred Qualifications: Experience providing technical guidance, peer review, or mentorship to less experienced analysts without formal supervisory responsibilities. Experience evaluating government laws, policies, enforcement efforts, and programs related to exploitative labor practices. Demonstrated ability to produce clear, well-supported analytical findings and recommendations for senior-level audiences. Professional Skills: Superb writing skills, including economic policy brief writing with an ability to tailor the tone, content and form of written output to different audiences and to suit a variety of formats; ability to synthesize information and communicate in an accurate and coherent manner. Humility to receive feedback, revise deliverables, and accept directions from others. Ability to think strategically, creatively and to find innovative ways to respond to emerging organizational and project needs. Detail-oriented and deadline-driven with strong organizational skills with an ability to work remotely. Ability to work in a dynamic environment with changing requirements and priorities. Strong cross-cultural, interpersonal, management, and collaboration skills in highly complex structures involving multiple teams and stakeholders. Critical thinking, sound problem solving, and decision-making skills. Highly self-motivated and able to work independently as well as in team settings. Capture and compile technical actions arising from panel deliberations, review findings, and follow-up decisions for project and government program leadership. Set the technical and analytical approach on key projects, challenge assumptions and take accountability for accurate, commercially robust and client-ready outputs. Lead or directly undertake the most complex elements of assignments where senior technical judgement is required. Direct and quality-assure work across lease reviews, maintenance cash-flow analysis, aircraft, engine and inventory valuations, fleet analysis, technical records, lease returns and transaction support. Provide end-to-end oversight of key assignments, ensuring clear scope and ownership, appropriate project set-up, disciplined work planning, visible client communications, timely technical review, accurate project documentation and effective management of budget and delivery risk. Guide analysts and multi-location delivery teams, resolving technical questions, providing constructive review and strengthening team capability. Advise clients on aircraft leasing, maintenance reserves, return conditions, MRO, asset management and aircraft lifecycle matters, resolving or escalating technical and delivery issues promptly. Develop, embed and maintain the methodologies, tools, templates and quality standards used across aircraft finance and technical advisory assignments. Develop team capability through structured coaching, technical review, practical training and progressive delegation of responsibility. Contribute technical expertise to proposals, client development and industry activity. Deep understanding of aircraft leases, maintenance reserves, return conditions, technical records, fleet maintenance obligations and aircraft lifecycle considerations. Demonstrated experience leading and quality-assuring complex analysis involving aircraft and engine assets, leases, maintenance cash flows, valuations or technical due diligence. Ability to supervise junior team members and multi-location delivery teams, providing clear technical direction and constructive feedback. Credibility and confidence to advise senior clients on complex technical and commercial aviation matters. Understanding of the requirements of lessors, airlines, lenders, investors and MRO providers in relation to aircraft assets. Excellent judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to identify technical risks, analytical inconsistencies and commercial implications. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex analysis into clear client advice. Ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines, locations and cultures. Willingness to travel for client meetings, inspections and project work as required. Experience working with aircraft lessors, lenders, investors, airlines, MROs, OEMs or technical service providers. Experience with aircraft appraisals, portfolio valuations, maintenance cash-flow forecasting, lease return and redelivery analysis, technical due diligence, asset-backed financing or aircraft transaction support. Experience reviewing lease documents, technical records, maintenance status reports, inspection outputs or maintenance-related assumptions used in valuation or transaction work.
